key_insight: Nanoindentation can trigger amorphous-to-bcc devitrification in refractory metal glasses, and their crystal-forming ability varies strongly across the series, with V most transformable and W most resistant.
engineering_relevance: This suggests mechanical contact loading can locally crystallize amorphous refractory coatings, so indentation resistance and long-term coating stability must be considered together in high-wear, high-temperature designs.
method: Melt-quenched amorphous V, Nb, Mo, Ta, and W to 300 K using molecular dynamics.
Validated interatomic potentials against ab initio liquid radial distribution functions.
Performed large-scale MD nanoindentation and tracked bcc fraction, nucleation, growth, and coalescence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a sigmoidal bcc-fraction-versus-depth response, a CFA range of about fourfold across elements, and a velocity scaling of CFA ∝ v^-1.08 with CFA·v nearly constant.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on MD with validated potentials, so quantitative trends may still depend on potential fidelity, loading conditions, and the simplified indentation geometry.
paper_title: Crystal forming ability of amorphous refractory metals under nanoindentation: a molecular dynamics study
